question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $38,$ the additive inverse of $16$ modulo $38$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $16$ modulo $38$ is the integer $0\le x<38$ such that

$$
x+16≡0\,(\text{mod}\,38).
$$

Notice that $-16+16≡0,$ so $x≡-16\,(\text{mod}\,38).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-16 & \,(\text{mod}\,38) \\  & ≡0-16 & \,(\text{mod}\,38) \\  & ≡38-16 & \,(\text{mod}\,38) \\  & ≡22 & \,(\text{mod}\,38)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $16$ modulo $38$ is $22.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
22+16≡38≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,38)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
